newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes up 1.85 at 993.20.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes up 1.85 at 993.20.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed up 1.85 at 993.20 after hitting the top of the central bank's daily floating rate exchange band and prompting the bank to intervene in the market by selling dollars, dealers said.

They attributed the peso's rise to a flood of dollars entering the country in the form of foreign credits and said dollar-selling by the Banco de la Republica early in the session did little to stop it.
Spokesmen for the central bank declined to comment on how much U.S. currency it sold when the peso hit its intra-day high of 993.15, the top of its exchange rate band for the day.

The bank -- which sees a strong currency as a shield against inflation -- has been under strong pressure to drive the peso lower. Its sharp appreciation since June has eroded the value of export revenues and helps make Colombian goods less attractive in global markets.
Much of the rise since late June, when the peso was trading at more than 1,070 to the dollar, has been attributed to an increase in petrodollars entering the country.
Dealers reported 260 trades in Tuesday's session for a total of $109.4 million and said the peso hit a session low of 995.15 before climbing higher. -- Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
